description: Osores Superbi is a five-member team combining data, development, research, design, and creative problem-solving. For NASA Space Apps 2026, we are working on Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data, exploring how NASA Earth observations and agricultural knowledge can help farmers make smarter, more resilient crop-rotation decisions.
summary:
🌾 Agroscope — Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data | NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026

🌍 Our Project

                            AGROSCOPE
Data from space. Better decisions on the ground.

Agroscope is a proposed AI-powered agricultural decision-support platform that connects NASA Earth Observation data with agricultural knowledge and farmer priorities.

Agroscope is designed to help farmers explore crop-rotation strategies that can:

🌱 Protect and improve soil health
💧 Use water and other resources more effectively
🌡️ Adapt to changing temperature and rainfall conditions
🌾 Consider crop characteristics and previous crops
⚠️ Identify potential agricultural risks
📊 Compare multiple possible crop-rotation strategies

The concept brings together information from NASA Earth observations, including datasets such as MODIS, SMAP, Landsat, GPM, and POWER, with agricultural information and farmer inputs.

Rather than replacing the farmer's judgment, Agroscope is designed to give farmers better information and multiple possible strategies to consider.

Agroscope is a web-based agricultural decision-support tool that connects NASA Earth observations with local agricultural knowledge and farmer priorities. It helps explore crop suitability, environmental risks, and crop-rotation strategies to support more climate-resilient farming. The platform is designed to turn complex data into clear, actionable insights for farmers, with English and Bangla support.
details:
AgroScope is an AI-powered, bilingual (English and Bangla) web-based decision support platform designed to help farmers navigate climate shifts and select optimal crop rotation systems.

  • User Profiling & Input: Farmers create a secure profile and provide key inputs such as their geographic division/location, land size, current crops, soil characteristics, and personal farming priorities.
  • AI & Geospatial Processing: The platform integrates farmer-submitted data with NASA Earth observation data (including MODIS, Landsat, ECOSTRESS, GPM, and NASA POWER) alongside soil and agricultural datasets (such as SoilGrids and FAO EcoCrop).
  • Actionable Insights Delivery: The system processes this through a geospatial analysis engine to output a complete interactive dashboard featuring a 3D globe visualization, climate and soil reports, risk assessments, side-by-side crop rotation comparisons, economic pros/cons, and a custom crop calendar—all guided by an interactive AI Field Helper and fully accessible in Bangla.
  • Data-Driven Precision: Replaces guesswork with space-grade satellite data and robust environmental analytics.
  • Resource Conservation & Resilience: Helps farmers protect fields, conserve water, and rebuild declining soil health over time against erratic rainfall and shifting temperatures.
  • Economic Clarity: Provides transparent rotation comparisons and economic analyses (pros and cons) to safeguard farm profitability.
  • Accessibility: Full language localization (Bangla support) and an intuitive AI assistant ensure the tool is approachable for local farmers regardless of technical background.
  • Enhance regional food security and community economic stability.
  • Mitigate the threats of climate change on vulnerable agricultural ecosystems.
  • Empower everyday farmers to adopt sustainable, long-term crop rotation practices that preserve land vitality for future generations.
  • Frontend: HTML, CSS, JavaScript.
  • Geospatial & Visualizations: CesiumJS (for immersive 3D geospatial mapping and earth observation layers) and SVG/Chart libraries for interactive data graphs.
  • Backend & Data Integration (Production Architecture): Python backend, connected via APIs to process satellite telemetry and agricultural datasets (NASA POWER, MODIS, Landsat, ECOSTRESS, GPM, SoilGrids, and FAO EcoCrop).
  • Development Environment: Modern web technologies and AI-assisted coding tools for rapid prototyping and iterative UI/UX design.
    AgroScope is creative because it recontextualizes macro-level scientific infrastructure—turning "NASA's eye in space"—into a micro-level, practical companion for a farmer in the field. Rather than overwhelming users with raw satellite feeds, it merges immersive 3D geospatial tech (CesiumJS) with an empathetic, bilingual conversational AI helper and localized agricultural reports, creating a seamless bridge between space technology and grassroots farming.
  • Accessibility & Language: Ensuring that farmers can interact effortlessly in Bangla with intuitive guidance from an AI Field Helper.
  • Scientific Grounding: Selecting credible, multi-source earth observation datasets (NASA, FAO, SoilGrids) to ensure high accuracy in climate and soil risk evaluations.
  • Practical Usability: Balancing deep technical data processing with a clean, easy-to-navigate dashboard that delivers clear economic and agronomic comparisons at a glance.
  • Scalability: Structuring a modular architecture capable of evolving from structured sample prototype data into a live, real-time API-driven backend.
